Why a longer deadline alone would be no fix, and the rule it follows: docs/solutions/testing/a-test-only-knob-widens-the-value-production-runs-pin-it-at-the-construction-a-deployment-reaches-INFRA-56.md says to make the bound an input rather than a wager on the machine, and never to widen a wall-clock bound instead. One run_processes poll walks /proc with a readlink, and often a grep, per process, so its cost belongs to the machine: at load ~370 with ~4,300 processes one walk outran the whole 30 s budget and until_true made a single attempt. The fix is therefore a poll floor — the wait gives up only once the deadline has passed AND it has polled at least MIN_POLLS times — with 600 s as the margin, not as the mechanism. The bounds are the function's own default arguments, so the script's call passes nothing and the test's third case reads the production default through the function a real run calls.

One property of the replaced wait is not carried over, deliberately: until_true aborts on $evidence/pane-endpoint-violation.txt.
